title: The threat scan: their checks, their captures

card.idea: Before you look for your own move, run a list for them. What checks do they have? What can they capture? What are they threatening next? Their checks first, because a check cannot be ignored.
card.habit: Look at the opponent's threats before your own idea.

explain.text: Start with their checks. Here Black has three squares to check on: f2, b4 and e4. You do not have to work out which is best. You only have to see that they exist.
Then their captures. Black can take on f3, on c3, on a2 and on f2. Four captures is a long list, and going through it is how you stop being surprised.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square Black could give check on with his next move.

hints.text: The queen has two of them and the bishop has two. One square is on both lists.
hints.text2: Your king is on e1. Look down the diagonal and along the file.

challenges.prompt: Tap every white piece Black could capture on his next move.

hints.text: The queen takes two of them and the bishop takes two.
hints.text2: Do not stop at the first one you see. There are four.

challenges.prompt: Black has exactly one check in this position. Tap the square he would give it on.

hints.text: Your king is on g1. Which black piece can land next to him?

challenges.reason: The bishop on d4 takes on f2, and that is check.

challenges.prompt: You have run Black's list. Now run your own and win material.

wrong.h3: A quiet move hands Black a free choice from his list of four captures.

hints.text: The black queen is standing on a square one of your knights already covers.

challenges.reason: Your knight on c3 attacks d5 and nothing of Black's defends the queen there.

challenges.prompt: A different board. Tap every white piece Black could capture on his next move.

hints.text: Only one black piece has a capture at all. Look at every square it can jump to.

challenges.prompt: The knight on e4 can take on f2 and on d2. How worried should you be?
options: Not worried. Both squares are defended, so either capture loses the knight.
Very worried. Both pawns are free.
Worried about f2 only. Nothing defends it.

hints.text: Listing a capture is not the same as fearing it. Count the defenders of each square.
hints.text2: Your rook and king both watch f2. Your queen, bishop and knight all watch d2.

challenges.reason: A capture on a defended square is on the list but it is not a threat. Listing it is still the right habit.

challenges.prompt: White takes the pawn on e5 with the knight. Is that safe?
reasons: No. The knight on c6 takes back.
No. The queen on d8 takes back.

hints.text: Run the scan for Black after your move, not before it.

takeaway: Checks, then captures, then threats — theirs before yours.
